readerQuestion: How should I use Home Assistant labels alongside areas and categories, and how can I check that a labeled action controls only the devices I intend?
directAnswer: Keep areas for physical rooms and use labels for shared purposes. For a precise first action, apply a new label directly to two working light entities, verify entity/device/area membership, and target only that label. Device or area labels may expand to additional controls, and combining a label with an area adds members rather than filtering them. Rehearse read-only first, then supervise a reversible two-lamp action.
originalContribution: Sections 1-5 build one explicit three-light, two-room membership plan, show a four-line read-only preview, provide an equivalent visual/YAML script, and compare label-only, area-only and combined targets with exact expected members. The troubleshooting table distinguishes wrong assignment level, action-domain mismatch, hidden entities, unavailable controls and unintended new membership. Seven synthetic registry cases exercised the unmodified upstream Core 2026.10.1 target-resolver function bodies: label only, area only, combined targets, two labels, hidden entity exclusion, a labeled two-channel device and a labeled area. This supports the worked example without claiming device testing.
limitations: Documentation and source-code research, not a running Home Assistant installation or hands-on lamp test. The resolver checks use in-memory registry fixtures and do not exercise transport, physical hardware, the Home Assistant UI or other household automations. The reader must verify their actual label ID, enabled/visible light entities, individual device response and absence of competing routines during the exercise. UI placement and hidden-target behavior are version-sensitive; source inspection is pinned to Core 2026.10.1. The generated cover is conceptual illustration. No indexing or traffic result is established by this review.

claimChecks.claim: Areas represent physical rooms; entities can carry multiple labels, and groups create a combined entity. The article retains room ownership and links to the existing Light Group guide for a shared control.
Labels can be created under Areas, labels & zones and assigned to selected entity rows. The procedure explicitly distinguishes the Entities tab from device/area labeling.
Categories organize their particular settings table and do not define the collection of lights an action should target.

label_entities returns only directly labeled entities; labels attached to devices or areas do not roll down into this function's result. An empty entity list alone does not establish an empty label-action target.
The read-only audit separately checks directly labeled devices, so a multi-channel device assignment is not overlooked.
The read-only audit separately checks labeled areas, preventing a whole-room assignment from being mistaken for two individual lamp assignments.
The script uses the actual internal label ID obtained from label_id rather than assuming the displayed name is valid YAML target syntax.
An action targets matching supported entities, and running it changes devices immediately. The example restricts the first command to light.turn_on with the label as its only target.

Core 2026.10.1 adds target selections together; label targets expand directly labeled entities and labeled devices/areas, while hidden entities are excluded from indirect expansion. The three-light outcome table and device/area examples matched seven synthetic resolver checks.
A script is a saved sequence with no trigger of its own; the YAML sequence can be run deliberately before any scheduled automation calls it.
